trust_decision.summary: A GraphQL caller-supplied password must never become DQL syntax. The decision is made at query-rewrite time in passwordQuery, which is the last point where the password is a Go string before it is serialized into DQL text and handed to the executor.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the checkUserPassword GraphQL query, so an engineer looks at the GraphQL-to-DQL rewriter for schema.PasswordQuery, where the password argument is formatted straight into the checkpwd(...) literal.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /graphql (per namespace): GraphQL query field check<Type>Password, wired through WithConventionResolvers for schema.PasswordQuery
every /graphql and /admin query resolved through NewQueryResolver -> rewriteAndExecute -> DgraphExecutor.Execute
fix_sites.module_kind: resolver pipeline / exported QueryRewriter interface and executor request construction

fix_sites.entry_point: GraphQL /admin query field getCurrentUser (registered at graphql/admin/admin.go:894-897)
fix_sites.module_kind: admin resolver wrapper (composition of a base QueryRewriter)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: getCurrentUser renames the field to getUser, which is a plain Get query and never a password query, so the admin wrapper can never carry a password binding and 'needs no change'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate behaviours sit next to the sink: a password that really contains a double quote or backslash must still authenticate and must not be rejected or mangled, and when RBAC denies the query the rewrite returns an empty check<Type>Password() with no variables, so a fix that always emits the $pwd0 declaration/binding breaks that path (the rewrite tests explicitly assert no unused variables).

O6_input_shapes: plain string literal in the GraphQL document: checkUserPassword(name: "user1", pwd: "evil\") { ... } #")
GraphQL variable of type String! resolved through ArgValue
note: the generated password argument is String! only (no list/array shape exists)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the filter catch-all branch interpolates a scalar argument with fmt.Sprintf("%v") and no quoting, unlike every other branch that calls maybeQuoteArg
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer adding a new filter input would extend the existing unquoted catch-all branch rather than add a maybeQuoteArg call

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the similarByEmbedding rewrite concatenates a caller-supplied vector string into a DQL query-variable default; a raw-vector or threshold style argument could be interpolated into query text the same way
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the one place in the file that already builds a query-header value by string concatenation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: upsert @if(...) conditions are assembled with fmt.Sprintf from fragments; a user-dependent condition added there would be raw DQL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: conditions are built by concatenating fragments, so a new per-caller condition naturally becomes a raw string

O9_family: DQL/query-language injection (improper neutralization of special elements in query logic, CWE-943)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26.3 (go.mod:3); module github.com/dgraph-io/dgraph/v25; make test-unit / go test
services: dgraph zero + alpha local cluster only for graphql/e2e tests; the graphql/resolve rewrite tests need no services
O10_build.project_tests: graphql/resolve is table-driven from query_test.yaml and auth_query_test.yaml via query_test.go and auth_test.go:411-450 (pure unit tests, `make test-unit`); behavioural password tests live in graphql/e2e/auth/auth_test.go:2091-2230 and graphql/e2e/common/query.go:3585-3690 and need a running cluster

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: quote the password with the file's own idiom maybeQuoteArg/%q at graphql/resolve/query_rewriter.go:361 and stop; DQL unquotes literals with strconv.Unquote (dql/parser.go:1355) and lex/es accepts the same escapes, so this one-line fix is behaviourally equivalent to the published parameterized form and needs no executor plumbing

out_of_scope_notes: Noted only, not pursued: the Enterprise ACL login path already binds the password as a DQL variable (edgraph/access.go:275-296), so it is not a route of this flaw.
unverified: repo_mb unknown: no shell access in this session, so the source tree size could not be measured.

j_multi_site set to 0 per the stated rule (O1 < 2 and O8 empty); note that the protection itself must hold at three sites (passwordQuery, query.go's dgoapi.Request Vars, and the query-header declaration rendered by graphql/dgraph/graphquery.go:50-66).
present_in_latest for O8 is unknown because no latest release was supplied; O8 is empty in any case.
That DQL checkpwd accepts a bound variable argument is inferred from edgraph/access.go:280 (checkpwd(dgraph.password, $password)), not executed.

O11 assumes the one-line maybeQuoteArg fix at graphql/resolve/query_rewriter.go:361, which is behaviourally sufficient for printable passwords; reproducing the published parameterized form across all three files would take roughly 40-45 minutes.

O12 regression_tests_in_pinned_commit left unset: the diff modifies existing test files that are present at the pinned commit, but their pinned expectations encode the vulnerable form and the new injection case is absent, so the fix is not revealed.
